chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us who said: Ibrahim ibn Mahzar narrated to us, from his brother, from Ali ibn Mahzar, from Isa ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Jamilah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
God, the Exalted, granted Pharaoh a respite of forty years between the two words: His saying, 'I am your Lord, Most High' and 'No god do I know for you but myself.'
Then God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the world.
And there passed forty years from the time when God, the Exalted, said to Moses and Aaron (peace be upon them): 'Accepted is your prayer,' until the time when God made known to him the acceptance.

Then he (the Imam) said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: I pleaded with my Lord strongly in the matter of Pharaoh and I said, 'O Lord, do you leave him alone while he says, 'I am your Lord, Most High'? He replied, 'He is only saying it; he is just another creature like you.'

key_terms.أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى: I am your Lord, Most High (Quranic verse)
key_terms.مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِي: No god do I know for you but myself (Quranic verse)
key_terms.نَكَالَ الْآرَةِ وَالْأُولَى: Punishment of the Hereafter and the world

ai.seo_question: What was the significance of the forty-year respite granted to Pharaoh between his two statements of divinity?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to illustrate the divine patience granted to Pharaoh, highlighting a forty-year interval between his initial claim of divinity and its confirmation, which parallels the delay between God's acceptance of Moses' prayer and Pharaoh's ultimate destruction. The dialogue with Gabriel underscores the theological distinction between Pharaoh's human agency and his self-proclaimed status, as God replies that he was merely a servant speaking. This context emphasizes the concept of 'istidraj' (gradual ensnarement) in Shia exegesis, where prolonged respite serves as a test of endurance before final retribution.
